Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration had no causal effect on depressive symptoms.
Sentence: "MR analysis revealed no causal effects of 25(OH)vitamin D concentration, either on DS (inverse variance weighted (IVW); b = 0.025, SE = 0.038, p = 0.52) or on BD (IVW; b = 0.020, SE = 0.012, p = 0.10)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (DS)
Population: Genetic summary data: 161,460 participants for depressive symptoms GWAS; SUNLIGHT GWAS of 79,366 subjects for 25(OH)D instruments
Intervention: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration (six SNPs)
Comparator: None (Mendelian randomization)
Design: other primary study
Sample size: 322,280
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Depressive symptom severity on the MADRS fell significantly from baseline to 12 weeks after a multicomponent personalized dietary program that included vitamin D3 supplementation.
Sentence: "At the endpoint, a significant reduction in depressive symptom severity was observed on the MADRS (from 15.52 ± 12.01 to 13.20 ± 11.66 points; p < 0.001) and HADS (from 17.00 ± 7.58 to 14.88 ± 7.82 points; p = 0.004)."
Measured as: depressive symptom severity (MADRS)
Population: 25 female patients with bipolar disorder or recurrent depression, mean age 31.3 years
Intervention: 12-week personalized dietary modification and nutrition education with targeted supplementation of omega-3, vitamin D3, magnesium and sodium butyrate
Comparator: none (single-arm, before vs after)
Design: case series
Sample size: 25
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
